messages.subject: nj tree
parts:
Hello group,
This is an attempt to get an nj tree output from a gl object:

gl:

/// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////

 // 282 genotypes,  29,915 binary SNPs, size: 65.6 Mb
 79443 (0.94 %) missing data

______________________________________________________
> gl.tree.nj(gl, type = "phylogram", outgroup = NULL, labelsize = 0.7)
Converting to a matrix of frequencies, locus by populations
Computing Euclidean distances
Error: vector memory exhausted (limit reached?)
_______________________________________________________

Is there limits for number of loci/genotypes?

gl:

/// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////

 // 282 genotypes,  29,915 binary SNPs, size: 65.6 Mb
 79443 (0.94 %) missing data

Thanks in advance for the help

Peco.

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: nj tree
parts:
Hi Peco,

Cannot see anything wrong with the script. Can you try the test script.

gl.tree.nj(testset.gl, type = "phylogram", outgroup = NULL, labelsize = 0.7)

If that works, then try

D <- gl.dist.pop(gl)

with your file and see if you get the error again.

Arthur

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: nj tree
parts:
Hi Peco,

This function is meant as a quick and dirty visualization. If you want to carry the analysis further, you should generate the distance matrix and pass it to something more sophisticated. However, added an option to output the tree topology in Newick format. See attached.

To visualize the tree using individuals, use

gl2 <- gl.reassign.pop(gl, as.pop="indNames(gl)")
gl.tree.nj(gl2)

Arthur
